Q: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement <package> A:

Try installing Flask through the PowerShell using the following command.

pip install --isolated Flask

This will allow the installation to avoid environment variables and user configuration.

Q: Python Package Installation Fails: 'Getting requirements to build wheel did not run successfully' A:

Your Python version is 3.13, and it is not compatible with Pillow 10.3.0. Pillow 10.3.0 supports Python 3.8 - 3.12. There aren't any Pillow wheels for Python 3.13.

So why did pip install pillow work? Installing a package without specifying a version usually attempts to install the latest release. So pip install pillow will give you the stable release of Pillow which supports Python 3.13.

Always look at the supported Python versions of specific packages and verify that the package version you are trying to install is compatible.

Q: How to script a u-boot partition? A:

I would try to copy the complete /dev/sda1 from the working card to your "manual" card.

cp /dev/sda1 working-sda1.img
...
cp working-sda1.img /dev/sda1

If that works, you could check which files are different.
If it fails, check the MBR or copy it also from the working card

Q: How to triage json.SemanticError when using encoding/json/v2? A:

JSONv2 author here.

It seems that you're asking for a way to distinguish between semantic errors due to the JSON input as opposed to a structural issue with the Go type. Both fall under the wider category of semantic errors, but we might want to provide a way to distinguish between the two. I suspect that almost all errors produced by encoding/json/v2/fields.go could be categorized as a "structural" error.

I recommend filing a feature request concretely explaining the use case. The initial release of v2 deliberately did not try to make it possible to distinguish every classification of errors since we didn't really know which ones people cared about.

Q: Why Getting Unknown [Error creating bean with name 'delegatingApplicationListener'] in spring security? Important A:

Spring Boot by default scan the full package and subpackages where the class annotated with @SpringBootApplication is located. Looking at your project structure, you have a bad package structure (the package io.spring.miniapi is not inside of io.demo.miniapi). Usually, in java applications with maven structure, you have a root package called [domain].[companyName] (io.demo.miniapi for your case) and then you create subpackages within it.

So knowing that, you have two options:

  1. Create the root package io.demo.miniapi and then inside create subpackages. Also, move your SpringBootMiniapiApplication.java to the root package.
  2. Use @ComponentScan in your SpringBootMiniapiApplication.java.
